newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND NEEDS POLICY ADJUSTMENT TO CAP C/A GAP-NOBE.
newsitem.headline: POLAND NEEDS POLICY ADJUSTMENT TO CAP C/A GAP-NOBE.

text.p: Poland needs to adjust its policies to stop a dangerously widening current account deficit, but recent floods and parliamentary elections are likely to postpone policy actions, the independent NOBE think-tank said.

"The necessary medium-run policy action is likely to be further postponed...(and) the unavoidable policy adjustment in the first half of 1998 will probably have to be much stronger than we previously assumed," the NOBE Independent Centre for Economic Studies said in its quarterly forecast for Reuters.
NOBE expects Poland's GDP to grow between 5.5 and six percent in 1997 despite a slowdown to below three percent in the third quarter caused by last month's catastrophic flooding.

"The government will have to face up to the challenge of increased budgetary pressure linked to additional flood-related spending and due to much higher costs of servicing the public debt," the report said.

NOBE said that the previously announced plans to cut next year's budget deficit to below two percent of GDP did not appear feasible because wage growth would probably not be sufficiently capped in 1997, an election year.
Poland will hold parliamentary elections on September 21.
NOBE said Poland's current account deficit would reach 5.5 percent of GDP in 1997, or more than $7 billion and that any further growth in 1998 could be dangerous.
In the first half of 1997 Poland posted a current account deficit of $2.697 billion, against a $272 million shortfall in the corresponding period of 1996.
